title: Inner Voices (Miniature I for solo viola)
program_note: Inner Voices (Miniature I for solo viola) was the first solo work I wrote while a doctoral student at Eastman School of Music.  Each of the pieces in the Miniatures series takes as its starting point and as its inspiration the unique sonic and technical capabilities of the single instrument.  Uniquely in this series, Inner Voices is in a particular key—in this case, the unusual (and difficult) E-flat minor, a key which for some reason I associate with having a Jewish flavor (it is the same key that I used for Prelude and Fugue No.12 from Parallel Universes: Preludes and Fugues for Prepared Piano and Piano Duo three decades later).  A clear melodic line is accompanied by one or two additional melodies in counterpoint.  These counterpoint lines—the “inner voices” so typical of the viola’s role in orchestral or chamber music—eventually reveal themselves to be the core of the piece.
